# kfilter default policy for Linux (kfilterd). The client is a Windows program run under
# Wine. kfilter names each Wine process by its Windows image (MapleStory.exe, not the Wine
# loader) and decides what the program does even when Wine does it for it: wineserver's
# file opens, socket connects, memory reads and signals for the program, winedevice's
# answers to its device requests, and its registry requests, are decided as the program's
# own and logged with the `brokered` flag (see docs/LINUX.md).
#
# Every layer Linux enforces is on, as in the Windows default policy: strict mode
# (default-deny: nothing without an allow rule), files and their metadata queries, registry,
# volume identity, network adapters, process creation, process memory, raw disk and network.
# The Linux-only rule-only layers (peer, thread-peer, system, dns, thread, /anon files and
# pipes, message) decide only what a rule names: here they are audited, and denied only where
# runs showed Wine and the client do not need them. Start in audit mode, run
# a full client session, review `kfilterctl watch`, add allow rules for what the client needs
# (Wine's own files, the prefix, the endpoints it uses), then switch with `kfilterctl on`.
# Switched on unreviewed, block mode stops the client. First match wins.
#
# Relaxations are counted where a run shows a fixed need (see policy/default-policy.txt):
#   allow|<target>|<exact path>|rights=...|uses=N[|phase=P][|opens][|image=<program>]
# and a deny can be limited the same way (`deny ... |uses=1` refuses the first request
# only). `image=` scopes any rule to one program: `image=grap-core64.aes`.
#
# Paths: Linux paths are case-sensitive and start with '/'; registry keys are NT names
# (\REGISTRY\MACHINE\..., any case); `*` is the only wildcard. kfilter names the opened file
# (symlinks resolved: /sys/class/net/* is /sys/devices/.../net/*), pseudo files /anon/<name>,
# and /proc/<pid> by whose process it is: /proc/@self, @family, @wine or @outside.
# `hide` on a deny makes its refusals look like a missing file (ENOENT).
#
# Placeholders: `monfilter.py run` replaces /@HOME@ with the user's home and /@WINEPREFIX@
# with the Wine prefix (default ~/.wine-nexon) before loading the policy. Loaded unfilled
# (kfilterctl policy on this file), those rules match nothing: their allows do not apply
# (more is refused, never less) and the launch root admits nothing.

mode audit
# The launch entry (`monfilter.py run` starts it under `kfilterctl launch`; --entry replaces
# this line with its own program): the user's start script, which runs `wine start`.
root /@HOME@/.local/bin/nexon-launcher
# The Windows programs to protect: every Nexon program (launcher, its Electron UI, agent and
# runtime, the NGS service, the game and its anti-cheat parts), matched on their Windows image
# (any case) wherever they are started: through `kfilterctl launch` or from the Nexon
# launcher. Their children inherit protection. In block mode with block-process-create, one
# started outside a launch is admitted only through the launch pass:
# `kfilterctl allow-launch nexon_client.exe`.
protect nexon_launcher.exe
protect nexon_client.exe
protect nexon_agent.exe
protect nexon_runtime.exe
protect NGService.exe
protect MapleStory.exe
protect DwarfAxe.exe
protect CrashReportClient.exe
protect grap-core64.aes
protect grap-updater.aes
protect grap-communicator64.aes

default-deny on
block-files on
# stat, access, readlink, xattrs and change watches (the denies below then also hide that a
# file exists; every allow also allows its metadata, and the directories above it are allowed
# `query` implicitly).
block-file-queries on
block-registry on
block-volume-serial on
block-network-adapter on
block-process-create on
block-process-memory on
block-raw-disk on
# No endpoint addresses have been reviewed: every connection is denied (would-deny
# in audit mode) until per-address allow rules are added (one host, port, tcp|udp,
# rights=connect, uses=N, risk=).
block-network on
network-default deny
network-loopback off
# Off: decisions on requests a Windows program makes with its own `syscall` instruction carry
# the `direct` flag either way; `on` refuses them all (Wine itself never makes one).
block-direct-syscall off

# ---- Never relaxed: identity, ahead of every allow ----

# Registry (from policy/default-policy.txt; Wine's user SID is S-1-5-21-0-0-0-<uid>).

deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\*ControlSet*\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\*ControlSet*\Services\Tcpip6\Parameters\Interfaces
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\NetworkList
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\*ControlSet*\Control\Class\{4d36e972-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\HARDWARE\ACPI

deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\*ControlSet*\Control\SystemInformation
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion|value=ProductId
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion|value=DigitalProductId*
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion|value=Install*
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion|value=Registered*

deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Diagnostics\DiagTrack
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SQMClient

deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\MountPoints2
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Valve
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Blizzard Entertainment
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Battle.net
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Epic Games

deny|file|/sys/devices/*/wwid

deny|file|/sys/devices/*/eui
deny|file|/sys/devices/*/serial_number
# Monitor EDID (serial, model, make); winex11 falls back without it.
deny|file|/sys/devices/*/edid|hide
deny|dir|/dev/disk/by-id
deny|dir|/dev/disk/by-uuid
deny|dir|/dev/disk/by-partuuid

deny|dir|/run/udev/data

deny|file|/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections
audit|file|/proc/cpuinfo
# The kernel, its modules, its build-id and the monitors (BPF LSM, BTF, pinned maps, tracing): not found.
deny|file|/proc/kallsyms|hide
deny|file|/proc/modules|hide
deny|file|/proc/version|hide
deny|file|/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease|hide
deny|file|/proc/sys/kernel/version|hide
deny|dir|/sys/kernel/security|hide
deny|file|/sys/kernel/security|hide
deny|dir|/sys/fs/bpf|hide
deny|dir|/sys/kernel/debug|hide

deny|dir|/sys/module|hide
deny|file|/sys/kernel/btf|hide
deny|dir|/sys/kernel/btf|hide
deny|file|/sys/kernel/notes|hide
# Other users' and other programs' processes: not found (Wine then reports their memory
# counters as 0). The program's own and the family's /proc entries are allowed below.
deny|file|/proc/@outside|hide
deny|dir|/proc/@outside|hide
# The gateway's MAC (ARP table), IPv6 interface ids and Wi-Fi state: open('/proc/net/arp') is
# /proc/<pid>/net/arp. Wine's GetIpNetTable is then empty and adapters lack IPv6 addresses. These
# /proc/*/net rules follow the hide above, so another program's tables still read as not found.
deny|file|/proc/*/net/arp
deny|file|/proc/*/net/if_inet6
deny|file|/proc/*/net/wireless
audit|file|/proc/*/net/route
# Every socket and address of the host (unix names kfilter's own /run/kfilter.sock), allowed below as
# the program's own /proc: Wine's TCP and UDP tables and IP statistics are then empty. Not net/dev: the
# game reads it around each channel change (the block loop's results).
deny|file|/proc/*/net/tcp
deny|file|/proc/*/net/tcp6
deny|file|/proc/*/net/udp
deny|file|/proc/*/net/udp6
deny|file|/proc/*/net/unix
deny|file|/proc/*/net/fib_trie
deny|file|/proc/*/net/packet
deny|file|/proc/*/net/netlink
deny|file|/proc/*/net/snmp
deny|file|/proc/*/net/snmp6
# Physical memory, I/O ports and CPU registers (MSRs, CPUID).
deny|file|/dev/mem
deny|file|/dev/kmem
deny|file|/dev/port
deny|file|/dev/cpu/*/msr
deny|file|/dev/cpu/*/cpuid
# The volume serial Wine reports for drive C: (block-volume-serial covers the filesystem's
# own UUID and label).
deny|file|/home/*/.wine*/drive_c/.windows-serial
deny|file|/home/*/.wine*/drive_c/.windows-label

# Windows inventory tools under Wine: the program they run is the PE image Wine loads, so
# they are refused as file reads (CreateProcess of them fails), whatever the loader is.
# `*` spans directories: this covers /opt/wine-*/lib/wine and distro Wine under /usr/lib*.
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/route.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/wmic.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/ipconfig.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/netsh.exe

deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/whoami.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/reg.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/regedit.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/winedbg.exe
deny|file|/*/wine/*-windows/powershell.exe
# Drivers the game does not use: Bluetooth (winebth reads BlueZ's adapters and devices over D-Bus and
# registers a pairing agent) and raw USB (wineusb). Audited, not refused: a refused load ends the
# winedevice.exe they share with winebus (Wine runs the driver anyway; linux_wine_test.sh).
audit|file|/*/winebth.sys|rights=execute|image=winedevice.exe
audit|file|/*/wineusb.sys|rights=execute|image=winedevice.exe

# Wine's NT objects that identify the machine (decided from wineserver open_file_object, as
# Windows' disk and device filters decide them): raw disks and volumes (disk serials, volume
# GUIDs), the mount manager (volume GUIDs, serials), NSI (adapters, MACs), HID/USB devices
# (vendor and product IDs), SCSI and optical drives. `*` spans '\'.
deny|file|\??\PhysicalDrive*
deny|file|\Device\Harddisk*
deny|file|\??\Harddisk*
deny|file|\??\Volume{*
deny|file|\Device\MountPointManager
deny|file|\??\MountPointManager
deny|file|\??\Nsi
deny|file|\Device\Nsi
deny|file|\??\HID#*
deny|file|\??\USB#*
deny|file|\??\SCSI*
deny|file|\??\CdRom*

# Escapes: services that run code or type keys outside the launch (no no_new_privs, not a
# descendant), credential agents, the microphone. Wine needs none of them.
deny|file|/dev/uinput
deny|file|/dev/snd/pcm*c
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/systemd/private
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/keyring/*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/gcr/*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/gnupg/*
deny|pipe|/home/*/.gnupg/*
deny|pipe|/tmp/ssh-*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/pipewire-0-manager
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/pk-debconf-socket
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/snapd-session-agent.socket
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/claude-*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/ccd-*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/cc-socks/*
deny|pipe|/run/user/*/discord-ipc-*

# Sound: these leave the client silent (other clients' pids and binaries, the microphone).
# deny|pipe|/run/user/*/pulse/native
# deny|pipe|/run/user/*/pipewire-0

# Name lookups go through the program's own port-53 query (decided as `dns`): the side
# resolvers are closed (glibc falls back to its own query). WPAD is never looked up.
deny|pipe|/var/run/nscd/socket|rights=connect
deny|pipe|/run/nscd/socket|rights=connect
deny|pipe|/run/systemd/resolve/io.systemd.Resolve|rights=connect
deny|pipe|/var/run/avahi-daemon/socket|rights=connect
deny|pipe|/run/avahi-daemon/socket|rights=connect
deny|dns|wpad
deny|dns|wpad.*

# System calls no Wine program needs: a secret memory area msmon cannot read, io_uring rings,
# and turning CPUID faulting off (keeps `monfilter.py run --trap-cpuid` armed; no effect
# without it).
deny|system|/system/secretmem
deny|system|/system/io_uring
deny|system|/system/arch_prctl/0x1012/1
# Executable memory files (memfds are allowed read and write below).
deny|file|/anon/memfd:*|rights=execute

# ---- Observed, never refused: the rule-only layers (no rule there means allowed and unlogged) ----

# One protected program reaching into another (memory writes, remote threads, thread context).
audit|peer|C:\*|rights=vm-write,vm-operation,create-thread
audit|thread-peer|C:\*|rights=get-context,set-context,suspend-resume
# Wine requests that enumerate the system or hide from a debugger.
audit|system|/system/wine/list_processes
audit|system|/system/wine/get_system_handles
audit|system|/system/wine/get_tcp_connections
audit|system|/system/wine/get_window_text
audit|system|/system/wine/get_directory_entries
audit|system|/system/wine/get_thread_context
audit|system|/system/wine/set_thread_context
audit|system|/system/wine/set_thread_info
# Host identity and kernel features (denying uname or sysinfo is safe for Wine; review first).
audit|system|/system/uname
audit|system|/system/sysinfo
audit|system|/system/socket/netlink/*/15
audit|system|/system/socket/packet
audit|system|/system/socket/inet/raw
audit|system|/system/socket/inet6/raw
audit|system|/system/userfaultfd
audit|system|/system/keyring
audit|system|/system/ipc
# Code written at run time: JIT, unpacked or injected (image/rx, Wine's copies of unaligned PE
# sections, is left out: noisy). Never deny private for nexon_client.exe (Chromium's V8).
audit|system|/system/memory/private
audit|system|/system/memory/shared
audit|system|/system/memory/image/rwx
# Calls Wine answers inside the program (a breakpoint in every Wine process for each function
# named: keep the list short; input polling such as NtUserGetAsyncKeyState is too hot).
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtUserBuildHwndList
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtUserFindWindowEx
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtUserInternalGetWindowText
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtUserSetWindowsHookEx
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtGdiBitBlt
audit|system|/system/win32k/NtGdiGetPixel
# WMI queries by class (a protected program loading wbemprox.dll stops a few ms until probed).
audit|system|/system/wmi/*
# Threads the anti-cheat modules start.
audit|thread|C:\*|module=grap*
# Every name looked up, and the first bytes sent on each connection (the TLS server name).
audit|dns|*
audit|message|rights=send|index=1
# Pipes a program outside the family made (a shell's pipe on stdin).
audit|pipe|/anon/pipe/@outside

# ---- Allowed: the Nexon family's own trees (image= keeps each to its programs) ----

# The game, its anti-cheat (grap) and overlay. The launcher patches it, so no image= here.
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/Nexon/Library/maplestorycw|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security|risk=anti-cheat-surface
allow|dir|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/Nexon/Library/maplestorycw|rights=enumerate,read,execute,write,delete,rename
# The launcher, its Electron UI (nexon_client), agent and runtime.
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Nexon/Nexon Launcher|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security|image=nexon_*
allow|dir|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Nexon/Nexon Launcher|rights=enumerate,read,execute,write,delete,rename|image=nexon_*
# NGService (Nexon Game Security) in %ProgramData%; the launcher installs and updates it.
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/ProgramData/Nexon/NGS|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security|image=NGService.exe|risk=anti-cheat-surface
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/ProgramData/Nexon|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security|image=nexon_*
allow|dir|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/ProgramData/Nexon|rights=enumerate,read,execute,write,delete,rename
# Per-user state and temp files.
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/users/*/AppData/Local/Nexon|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/users/*/AppData/Roaming/Nexon|rights=read,write,execute,delete,rename,set-security
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/users/*/AppData/Local/Temp|rights=read,write,delete,rename
# Settings in the registry (as on Windows).
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Nexon|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Nexon|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Nexon|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\USER\*\Software\Wizet|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wizet|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate

# Network: REVIEW REQUIRED. No Nexon endpoint is allowed yet, so every connection is denied
# (would-deny in audit mode). Take the endpoints from a run's tuning report, then add one
# counted rule per host, e.g.:
#   allow|network|ip=<host>/32|port=443|proto=tcp|rights=connect|uses=N|risk=<reason>|image=nexon_client.exe

# ---- Allowed: what Wine itself needs to start ----

# Read and run Wine, the libraries and the prefix's Windows directory; write only the
# prefix's own state. Narrow these from the tuning report once a run is reviewed.
allow|file|/opt/wine-stable|rights=read,execute
allow|file|/usr/lib|rights=read,execute
allow|file|/usr/share/fonts|rights=read
allow|file|/usr/share/zoneinfo|rights=read
allow|file|/etc/fonts|rights=read
allow|file|/etc/ld.so.cache|rights=read|exact
allow|file|/etc/localtime|rights=read|exact
allow|file|/dev/null|rights=read,write|exact
allow|file|/dev/urandom|rights=read|exact
# Pseudo files: memfds (Mesa, xshmfence, PulseAudio), private MIT-SHM segments and shared
# anonymous memory. Their exec and keyed SysV segments are denied above.
allow|file|/anon/memfd:*|rights=read,write
allow|file|/anon/SYSV00000000|rights=read,write
allow|file|/anon/dev/zero|rights=read,write
deny|file|/anon/SYSV*
# Its own and the family's /proc entries (maps, stat, status, fd links); Wine's other
# processes are logged.
allow|file|/proc/@self|rights=read,query
allow|dir|/proc/@self|rights=read,enumerate,query
allow|file|/proc/@family|rights=read,query
allow|dir|/proc/@family|rights=read,enumerate,query
audit|file|/proc/@wine
audit|dir|/proc/@wine
# The /proc/self link itself (realpath walks) and the names of its own threads.
allow|file|/proc/self|rights=query|exact
allow|file|/proc/thread-self|rights=query|exact
allow|file|/proc/@self/task/*/comm|rights=read,write,query
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/windows|rights=read,execute
allow|dir|/@WINEPREFIX@/drive_c/windows|rights=enumerate,read,execute
allow|file|/@WINEPREFIX@/dosdevices|rights=read
allow|dir|/@WINEPREFIX@/dosdevices|rights=enumerate,read
# Other Wine prefixes: after the prefix's own allows, which win when the run's prefix is ~/.wine.
deny|file|/home/*/.local/share/wineprefixes|data-only
deny|file|/home/*/.wine|data-only

# Wine's NT objects it needs: sockets go through AFD, the console through ConDrv, and Wine's
# services (plugplay, the service manager, RPC, OLE) talk over named pipes.
allow|file|\Device\Afd|rights=read,write,open
# Named sections (shared memory by name) Wine itself opens: the shared user data page, the code
# page tables and its preloaded system DLLs. Any other name (\Sessions\*\BaseNamedObjects\...:
# shared memory with, or a probe for, another program) is refused in block mode.
allow|file|\KernelObjects\__wine_user_shared_data|rights=read,write,execute,delete,set-security,open
# win32u's session data: every graphical Wine program reads it (refused, no window opens).
allow|file|\KernelObjects\__wine_session|rights=read,open
allow|file|\NLS\*|rights=read,open
allow|file|\KnownDlls*|rights=read,execute,open
allow|file|\Device\ConDrv*|rights=read,write,open
allow|file|\??\CONIN$|rights=read,write,open
allow|file|\??\CONOUT$|rights=read,write,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\wine_plugplay|rights=read,write,create,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\svcctl|rights=read,write,create,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\lrpc\*|rights=read,write,create,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\net\NtControlPipe*|rights=read,write,create,open
# The Nexon family's own IPC: Chromium (mojo) and Node (uv) inside the launcher, the anti-cheat
# with the game, the overlay with the game. Other pipes are refused in block mode.
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\mojo.*|rights=read,write,create,open,set-security
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\uv\*|rights=read,write,create,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\grap-core*|rights=read,write,create,open
allow|pipe|\??\pipe\DwarfIPCPipe*|rights=read,write,create,open

# Connecting to the prefix's wineserver (every Wine process does at start).
# Wine's per-user server directory: the lock file wineserver takes at start.
allow|file|/tmp/.wine-*|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security
# ... and its directory, which every Wine process stats before it connects (block-file-queries).
allow|dir|/tmp/.wine-*|rights=read,enumerate,query
allow|pipe|/tmp/.wine-*/server-*/socket|rights=connect
# Process creation: Wine's loaders and the ELF interpreters they start, nothing else. The
# path is the file that is executed (symlinks resolved: /usr/bin/wine is /usr/lib/wine/...).
allow|process|/opt/wine-stable|rights=create
allow|process|/opt/wine-staging|rights=create
allow|process|/opt/wine-devel|rights=create
allow|process|/usr/lib/wine|rights=create
allow|process|/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2|rights=create|exact
allow|process|/usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/ld-linux.so.2|rights=create|exact
allow|process|/usr/lib/ld-linux.so.2|rights=create|exact
# The launch entry script and the interpreter its #! line names (/usr/bin/env bash).
allow|process|/@HOME@/.local/bin/nexon-launcher|rights=create|exact
allow|process|/usr/bin/env|rights=create|exact
allow|process|/usr/bin/bash|rights=create|exact
# Add process allows above this line: nothing below it is ever reached for an exec.
deny|process|/*
